topic: A Pen-Cap Hole Is an Airway Safety Feature
creativeBrief:
Pattern: CONTRADICTION_REVEAL_V4. Audience: global English-speaking viewers; state country, model and time scope naturally. Channel angle: familiar objects with a surprising but true job. Generate five declarative, concrete subject-first hooks. For this topic prefer 10–12 spoken words so the opening has enough measured time before the late reveal; do not give away the mechanism at once. Six story functions across five voiced scenes: visual paradox, contradiction, clue, mechanism, distinct second reveal, payoff. Target 25–29 seconds including the configured sign-off; hard max 30. Keep voice, karaoke, local BGM and channel outro. No generic spoken CTA. Visual direction: Use the photoreal live-action style in visualStyle, like varied Pexels-style footage. Open on the real object and its surprising visible detail. Build five distinct camera setups: vary at least two of shot scale, angle, location, lighting and physical action between neighboring scenes. Prefer observable actions, practical macro details, human hands, and real-world context over abstract visual metaphors. For a hidden mechanism, use a plausible exposed component or demonstration prop without pretending an invented event was filmed. Keep brand signs out if accurate rendering is doubtful. Generate a distinct Gemini still and Google Flow six-second clip per voiced scene; review action, 9:16 crop and continuity before binding local MP4s. Generated shots explain sourced facts and are not documentary proof. Packaging: make the YouTube title and description curiosity-driven, a little provocative, and specific to the subject; deliver exactly the claim the video explains. The title may tease the mechanism, but do not exaggerate risk, savings, universality or a company motive beyond the facts. The description should invite one topic-specific viewer response.
Pen-cap timing design: This topic has failed measured V5 timing twice because a 7–8-word opening and a short clue put the mechanism near 6s, while a wordy ISO 11540 mechanism exceeded the six-second Flow source. Plan a roughly 3.4–3.8s opening, 5.3–5.7s clue, 5.3–5.7s mechanism, 4.5–5s second reveal, and 4–4.5s payoff; the fixed channel outro is measured separately. Those are desired spoken durations including the normal audio tail, not silent holds or padded visuals. The mechanism must begin at or after 7s; the second reveal at or after 14s; each non-opening scene must use at most 5.8s of its six-second source. Keep the selected hook verbatim through any rewrite. Give the clue a meaningful observable action and full sentence: turning the real cap toward light makes the through-hole legible; do not invent an accident or test. Keep the mechanism concise: say that the certified vented BIC cap is intended to reduce asphyxiation risk, but leave the long standard number for the second reveal or short display copy. The second reveal states that ISO 11540 applies to writing-instrument caps likely to be used by children up to fourteen. The payoff makes clear this is risk reduction, not guaranteed breathing, and not every cap is vented. Aim for roughly 70 spoken words including the configured sign-off, with substance concentrated in the clue instead of overloading mechanism. Do not speak punctuation or unnatural numerical strings just to fill time. Treat these as timing and fact constraints, not an exact script.
YouTube title seed: The Tiny Hole in a Pen Cap Has a Serious Job
YouTube description seed: It looks like a stray design detail, but vented caps can meet a child-safety standard. Had you noticed that hole before? #TellMeWhyyyyyy #Shorts
Core fact: BIC’s Cristal Expression cap is certified to ISO 11540, a standard intended to reduce asphyxiation risk from writing-instrument caps.
Second reveal: ISO 11540 covers caps for writing instruments likely to be used by children up to age 14.
Opening shot: a real vented pen cap in a hand, with the hole plainly visible. Show it as a believable real-world shot, immediately legible in the first frame. Do not reveal the internal mechanism in the opening. Use different real camera compositions and meaningful subject motion for the clue, mechanism, second reveal and payoff. Do not use an imaginary accident, simulated rescue, or fake news-style scene. 
Fact boundaries: The standard aims to reduce risk, not guarantee breathing or make accidental inhalation safe. Scope BIC compliance to the certified Cristal Expression cap; do not imply every pen cap has a vent. Do not depict a choking reenactment.
